comments.text_zh: 如果你想用电来供暖，它们很棒，因为效率是电阻式加热器的 3 到 4 倍。这取决于你所在地区的电价和其他热源。如果你住在气温会低于 -15 摄氏度的北方，空气对空气机组就没那么好，因为室外越冷，它们效率越低。我的热泵 COP 为 3，意思是它能用 1/3 的电量产生和电阻式加热器一样多的热量，但它在 -15 摄氏度时会停机，因为低于这个温度，它的效率就不如电阻式加热。如果你的热泵 COP 为 4，可能要到 -25 摄氏度才会变得不如电阻式加热器高效。更好但更贵的热泵使用地源水，水可以来自两口井，或来自不会冻到底的深池塘，或来自草坪下方埋得足够深、冬天不会冻结的许多米长的水管。由于深度，它们总能获取地热，所以在冬天不会损失效率。Technology Connections 的 YT 频道有几个不错的视频讲解它们是如何工作的：1. [VIDEO] 2. [LINK]
comments.text: They are great if you are looking to use electricity to heat because they are 3 to 4 times more efficient than resistive heaters. It depends on the price of electricity and other heat sources in your area. If you live in the north where temperatures go below -15 Celsius, air-to-air units aren't as great because they lose efficiency as it gets colder outside. My heat pump has a COP of 3, meaning it can generate as much heat as a resistive heater using 1/3 the electricity, but it shuts off at -15 Celsius because below that point it is less efficient than resistive heat. If your heat pump has a COP of 4, you might get to -25 Celsius before it is less efficient than a resistive heater. Better, but more costly, heat pumps use in-ground water, either from a pair of wells, or from a deep pond that won't freeze to the bottom, or from many meters of water pipe buried deep enough beneath your lawn to not freeze in the winter. Because of the depth, they always have access to the earth's heat so they don't lose efficiency in the winter. The Technology Connections YT channel has a couple of good videos about how them: 1. [VIDEO] 2. [LINK]

comments.text_zh: 这位[0]做过好几期关于热泵的深度讲解，澄清了不少误解（比如热泵在寒冷天气下不管用）。如果你正考虑装热泵，这些内容挺有意思的。我一直觉得这事挺荒唐：冬天我们花钱给房子供暖，却在屋里花钱维持一个冷箱子（冰箱）；夏天我们花钱给房子降温，却又花大把钱去加热烘干机、炉灶等等。看了这些视频让我觉得，将来完全有可能出现某种全屋热泵，只是把热量从它现在所在的地方搬到你需要的地方，从而减少各个系统互相拆台、分别给房子某些区域加热／制冷的需要。我知道商用领域有具备这种能力的东西，但一时想不起叫什么名字。0: [VIDEO] 1: [LINK]
comments.text: This guy[0] has done quite a few deep dives on heat pumps that cover a lot of the myths (eg they don't work in the cold). It's pretty interesting material if you're thinking about a heat pump. It has always seemed silly to me that we spend money to keep a box of cold (fridge) inside the houses we're spending money to heat in the winter and spend a lot of money to heat up dryers, stoves, etc in the houses we're spending money to cool in the summer. Watching these videos made me think there's a real possibility at some point to have something like a whole home heat pump that just moves heat from where it is to where you want it and in the process reduces the need for systems working against each other to heat/cool specific parts of the house. I understand there's something in commercial settings that has this capability but I'm blanking on the name. 0: [VIDEO] 1: [LINK]
